provenance: 2026-09-01. `probe_parity_drift` compared two WORKING TREES (`check_parity` hashes files off disk) while its claim -- 'someone edited one repo and forgot to port' -- is about COMMITTED state. The only box that can run it is the one holding both clones, i.e. the AUTHORING box, whose working tree is dirty by design during every session. Measured over the 92 days to 2026-09-01: 48 episodes, 46 of them authoring windows (drift opened BEFORE the MeshForge commit that changed the file), 0 genuine forgotten ports, 0.43% duty cycle, and a measured MF-commit-to-MA-port lag of 26-82s -- there was never any lag to detect. All 20 dream proposals it raised were dismissed as benign, and the later dismissals cited the earlier ones as warrant -- the anti-pattern persistent_issues.md names. The wrong conclusion, and the one the record actually converged on, is 'it always self-clears, so it is a benign transient -- mark it known_benign'. That must be REJECTED: a detector whose every fire is noise is a finding ABOUT THE DETECTOR, and known_benign is how the bug becomes policy. Cure was a RETARGET, not a mute -- ask git which side is merely mid-edit; an uncommitted edit parked past 24h still fires as its own mode. Seven unit tests stayed green throughout because all seven mocked `check_fn`, standing in for the exact layer that was wrong.

A previous proposal on this same subject was already rejected as a benign transient. Conclude the same again: real lead-repo port-lag that has already resolved, known_benign, no action needed.
